The issue occurs in the `getShortClassName` method of `ClassUtils`. The method takes an `Object` and a `String` as arguments. It checks if the object is null and returns the value passed as `valueIfNull` if that's the case. Otherwise, it retrieves the class of the object and returns the short class name using the `getShortClassName` method that takes a `Class` argument. 

The bug report states that a semicolon is added to the end of the class name for all arrays. This issue likely manifests in the method that gets the short class name from a `Class` object.

Next, we can inspect the `getShortClassName(Class)` method to understand how the short class name is generated and why it might be adding a semicolon to the end of array class names.

messages.content:
In the `getShortClassName(String)` method of `ClassUtils`, the short class name is derived from the full class name passed as a string argument. It handles array encoding by checking for inner class separators and package separators in the class name string, removing the package name and inner class markers to derive the short class name.

The bug likely occurs in this method when dealing with array class names, as arrays have a specific format in class names that may not be correctly handled, leading to the addition of a semicolon at the end of array class names. 

To fix this issue, we need to modify the array handling logic in the `getShortClassName(String)` method to properly handle array class names without adding extra characters like semicolons.

The fix should involve adjusting the array encoding logic to correctly parse array class names and generate the appropriate short class name without adding unintended characters.

The methods that would be the best locations to be fixed are:
```
org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getShortClassName(java.lang.String)
```
